title: Jacky Chou on 9 income streams: agency, dropshipping, FBA, content sites and newsletters
summary: Jacky walks through every business model he has run, with the real numbers, pros, cons and mistakes. Key lessons: use your own assets as case studies to sell services, avoid correlated risk across content sites, and prefer newsletters for their lack of platform risk.

principles.text: Optimize for income that arrives while you're away, not billable hours, even at high hourly rates.
principles.quote: you should be trying to make money when you're out golfing for example or when I'm at the gym money's still coming in. I'll get stripe notifications.

principles.text: Sell agency services by building your own asset as a case study and talking about it openly; clients then come inbound.
principles.quote: I think you should have a case study, so you should build up an asset via SEO and just talk about it. And then clients will just start flowing in.

principles.text: Agencies give great cash flow but margins compress as you add headcount; keep yours deliberately lean.
principles.quote: Pros, cash flow, it's great. You get paid right away. Cons, margin.

principles.text: If clicks are cheap but sales are low, the problem is conversion, not ads or targeting. Fix the site first.
principles.quote: if you have like low cost per clicks on Facebook, it's not the ad problem. It's not a targeting problem cuz people are clicking, they're just not converting.

principles.text: Rolling up many risky assets only diversifies if they use different tactics; shared tactics mean correlated failure.
principles.quote: when the same person operates these 10 different businesses and utilizes the same tactics, the risk is still there.

principles.text: Newsletters are attractive because you own the audience, with no platform dependency, unlike Amazon, Facebook or Google traffic.
principles.quote: I love the business model because there's no platform risk.
